site_number: Land and buildings at Commerce Road Industrial Estate
application_type_full: Outline planning permission: Some matters reserved
description: The repair, restoration, conversion and extension of retained elements of the existing warehouse buildings to provide residential (C3), business (B1); waterside restaurant/cafe (A3/A4) and waterside leisure and community uses (D1/D2) with associated plant, servicing and storage. Retention of 'art deco' frontages to provide business (B1) uses. Redevelopment of bus depot to provide improved facilities. Redevelopment of remaining land to provide residential (C3), business (B1), leisure/community (D1/D2), restaurant/cafe (A3/A4) uses with associated landscaping, access, parking, supporting infrastructure and pedestrian/cycle bridge (Outline application).
decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - Time Limit
The development hereby permitted shall be
begun either before the expiration of three
years from the date of this permission or
before the expiration of two years from the
date of approval of the last of the reserved
matters to be approved, whichever is the
later.

Condition : 2 - Approved Plans
The proposed development shall be carried
out in all respects in accordance with the
proposals contained in the application
(attached schedule) and the plans submitted
therewith or as shall have been otherwise
approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority before the buildings are occupied.

Condition : 3 - Phasing
Prior to commencement of development a
Phasing Plan shall be submitted to and
approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority. The phasing of the development
shall be carried out in accordance with the
approved phasing plan, unless an
alternative phasing plan is first submitted to
the Local Planning Authority with an
assessment of any effects, including any
different impacts on the environment, and
that alternative plan and assessment is
approved by the Local Planning Authority
pursuant to this condition.

Condition : 4 - Flood Defenses
Development hereby permitted shall not be
commenced until such time as a scheme to
ensure access to and maintenance of
existing flood defences has been submitted
to, and approved in writing by, the Local
Planning Authority. The development shall
be carried out in accordance with the details
so approved.

Condition : 5 - Phased Contamination Condition
Before the development hereby permitted
commences:
a. A contaminated land Phase 1 desk
study report shall be submitted to,
and approved in writing by the Local
Planning Authority. Should the
Phase 1 report recommend that a
Phase 2 site investigation is
required, then this shall be carried
out and submitted to, and approved
in writing by the Local Planning
Authority. The site shall be
investigated by a competent person
to identify the extent and nature of
contamination. The report should
include a tiered risk assessment of
the contamination based on the
proposed end use of the site.
Additional investigation may be
required should it be necessary.
b. If required, a scheme for
decontamination of the site shall be
submitted to the Local Planning
Authority, for written approval. The
scheme shall account for any
comments made by the Local
Planning Authority before the
development hereby permitted is
first occupied.
During the course of the development:
c. The Local Planning Authority shall be
notified immediately if additional
contamination is discovered during
the course of the development. A
competent person shall assess the
additional contamination, and shall
submit appropriate amendments to
the scheme for decontamination in
writing to the Local Planning
Authority for approval before any
work on that aspect of development
continues.
Before any phase of the development is first
brought into use:
d. The agreed scheme for
decontamination referred to in
clauses b) and c) above, including
amendments, shall be fully
implemented and a written
validation (closure) report submitted
to the Local Planning Authority for
approval.

Condition : 6 - Foul and Surface Water
The development hereby permitted shall not
be commenced until such time as a scheme
to dispose of foul and surface water has
been submitted and approved in writing by,
the local planning authority. The scheme
shall be implemented as approved as
approved for the relevant phase.

Condition : 7 - SUDS
Prior to the commencement of development
approved by this planning permission (or
such other date or stage in development as
may be agreed in writing with the Local
Planning Authority), a surface water
drainage scheme for the site, based on
sustainable drainage principles and an
assessment of the hydrological and
hydrogeological context of the development,
has been submitted to and approved in
writing by the local planning authority. The
scheme so approved shall be fully
implemented and subsequently maintained,
in accordance with the timing / phasing
arrangements embodied within the scheme,
or within any other period that may
subsequently be agreed, in writing, by the
local planning authority.

Condition : 8 - Archaeological Work
No development shall take place until the
applicant has provided a strategy for the
implementation of a programme of
archaeological work (including field evaluation
and a subsequent mitigation strategy, if
necessary) in accordance with a written scheme
of investigation which has been submitted by
the applicant and approved by the Local
Planning Authority and the programme shall be
carried out as approved .

Condition : 9 - Water Supply Impact Study
Development shall not commence until
impact studies of the existing water supply
infrastructure have been submitted to and
approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority. The studies shall determine the
magnitude of any new additional capacity
required in the system and a suitable
connection point as well as a timetable for
implementation. The development shall
thereafter be implemented in accordance
with the approved details.

Condition : 10 - Access Strategy
Prior to commencement of development, a
site-wide access strategy for the Application
Site shall be submitted to and approved in
writing by the Local Planning Authority.
This shall include:
a) how access shall be provided into
and around the site for all modes of
transport (excluding the individual
Development Zones);
b) the location of on-street parking
spaces; and
c) the location of bus stops along
Commerce Road
Each part of the development shall conform
to the strategy so approved

Condition : 11 - Landscape Strategy
No development shall take place until a sitewide
landscape masterplan (excluding
Robin Grove Recreation Ground and the
footbridge) has been submitted to and
approved in writing by the local planning
authority.

Condition : 12 - Construction Environmental Management
Plan
A Construction Environmental Management
Plan shall be submitted to and approved in
writing by the Local Planning Authority prior
to the implementation of development. The
construction of the proposed development
shall then be carried out in accordance with
the details set out within the approved
Construction Environmental Management
Plan.

Condition : 13 - Construction Logistics Plan
No development shall commence until a
site-wide Construction Logistics Plan has
been submitted to the Local Planning
authority and approved in writing. The CLP
should include for the relevant phase:
a) booking systems
b) consolidated or re-timed trips
c) secure, off-street loading and drop-off
facilities
d) using operators committed to best
practice, demonstrated by
membership of TfL?s Freight Operator
Recognition Scheme (FORS), or
similar.

Condition : 14 - Plan for the Provision of Solar Photovoltaic
Panels
Prior to the commencement of development,
a plan setting out the general location of no
less than 800 sqm of roof mounted solar
photovoltaic panels with a southern
component and absent of significant
shading throughout the year shall be
submitted to and approved in writing by the
Local Planning Authority. These shall then
be implemented in accordance with the
approved layout unless otherwise agreed in
writing with the Local Planning Authority.

Condition : 15 - Plan for Green Roofs
Prior to the commencement of development,
a plan setting out the location of green roofs
shall be submitted to and approved in
writing by the Local Planning Authority.
This shall demonstrate how at least 30% of
the roofs constructed pursuant to the
planning permission will be green roofs.
These shall then be implemented as
approved or as amended by agreement with
the Local Planning Authority at the
Reserved Matters Application stage

Condition : 16 - Bird Hazard Management Plan
Development shall not commence until a
Bird Hazard Management Plan has been
submitted to and approved in writing by the
Local Planning Authority. The submitted
plan shall include details of:
a) management of any flat/ shallow
pitched/ green roofs on buildings
within the site which may be attractive
to nesting, roosting and ?loafing?
birds. The management plan shall
comply with Advice Note 8 ?Potential
Bird Hazard from Building Design?.
The Bird Hazard Management Plan shall be
implemented as approved on completion of
development and shall remain in force for
the life of the development. No subsequent
alterations to the plan are to take place
unless first submitted to and approved in
writing by the Local Planning authority.

Condition : 17 - Construction Works
No demolition or construction work shall
take place on the site except between the
hours of 8am to 6pm on Mondays to Friday
and 9am to 1pm on Saturdays and not at all
on Sundays and Public Holidays without the
prior written approval of the Local Planning
Authority.

Condition : 18 - Penetrative Methods
Prior to any piling works, installation of
Ground Source Heat Pumps or any other
foundation designs using penetrative
methods being undertaken, written consent
shall be obtained from the Local Planning
Authority.. The development shall be carried
out in accordance with the details to which
the authority has given its consent.

Condition : 19 - Remediation Strategy
Prior to occupation of any part of the
permitted development, a verification report
demonstrating completion of the works set
out within the Remediation Strategy
required by Condition 5 and the
effectiveness of the remediation shall be
submitted to and approved, in writing, by
the local planning authority. The report shall
include results of sampling and monitoring
carried out in accordance with the approved
verification plan to demonstrate that the site
remediation criteria have been met. It shall
also include any plan (a long-term
monitoring and maintenance plan) for
longer-term monitoring of pollutant
linkages, maintenance and arrangements for
contingency action, as identified in the
verification plan, and for the reporting of
this to the local planning authority. The
plan so approved shall be adhered to.

Condition : 20 - Contingency Action
If required by the Remediation Strategy
approved under Condition 19, reports on
monitoring, maintenance and any
contingency action carried out in
accordance with a long-term monitoring and
maintenance plan shall be submitted to the
local planning authority as set out in that
plan. On completion of the monitoring
programme a final report demonstrating that
all long- term site remediation criteria have
been met and documenting the decision to
cease monitoring shall be submitted to and
approved in writing by the local planning
authority.

Condition : 21 - Delivery and Servicing Plan
No part of the development shall be
occupied until a site-wide Delivery and
Servicing Plan has been submitted to and
approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority. This shall then be implemented
as approved and remain in operation for the
lifetime of the development.

Condition : 22 - Maximum Floorspace
The total floorspace areas of the uses
hereby approved shall be limited to the
following:
a) overall floorspace area of all the uses
shall not exceed 77,557sqm Gross
Internal Area (GIA) and 79,887 sqm
Gross External Area (GEA);
b) residential floorspace (Class C3) shall
not exceed 51,565 sqm GIA and
53,150 GEA;
c) commercial floorspace (Class B1)
shall not exceed 6,780 sqm GIA and
7,000 sqm GEA;
d) restaurant and caf? floorspace (Class
A3/A4) shall not exceed 840 sqm GIA
and 860 sqm GEA;
e) leisure and community floorspace
(Class D1/ D2) shall not exceed 840
sqm GIA and 860 sqm GEA;
f) bus depot (including workshop and
office floorspace) floorspace (Use
Class Sui Generis) shall not exceed
2,107 sqm GEA;
g) parking, plant and storage (Use Class
Sui Generis) floorspace shall not
exceed 15,185 sqm GIA and 15,660
sqm GEA;
h) energy centre (Use Class Sui Generis)
floorspace shall not exceed 240 sqm
GIA and 250 sqm GEA.

Condition : 23 - Maximum Number of Residential Units
The residential accommodation hereby
approved shall not exceed 520 units overall.

Condition : 24 - Housing Mix
Unless otherwise agreed in writing by the
Local Planning Authority the development
shall include not less than 35% of units as
three or more bedroom accommodation.

Condition : 25 - Maximum Parking Provision
The car parking provided on the site shall
not exceed a maximum of 430 spaces and
the cycle parking provided on the site shall
not exceed 586 spaces. This parking shall
be provided in accordance with Table 3.13 of
Document SD2 (provided at Appendix x).

Condition : 26 - Disabled Parking
A minimum of 33 of the parking spaces
hereby approved shall be suitable for the
use of wheelchair users. These spaces shall
be laid out in a location and in a manner that
shall first be submitted to and approved in
writing by the local planning authority.

Condition : 27 - Lifetime Homes
All of the residential units will comply with
the Lifetime Homes Standard.

Condition : 28 - Wheelchair Units
10% of the residential units will be designed
to be wheelchair accessible, or easily
adaptable for wheelchair users.

Condition : 29 - Single Aspect Noise
No single aspect residential units shall be
provided within those locations falling
within Noise Exposure Category NEC C of
PPG24.

Condition : 30 - Floor Levels
Finished floor levels of the development
shall be set no lower than 6.957m AOD.

Condition : 31 - Building Heights
No building or any part of the development
hereby permitted shall exceed the specified
height AOD as set out in) Document SD2:
Development Specification and Place-
Making Principles (as amended 7th February
2011); and
Document SD3 Regulatory Plans (as
amended 7th February 2011) and no louvre,
ducts or other external plant equipment
shall be installed on any building without
the prior written approval of the Local
Planning Authority.

Condition : 32 - Ensuring a Reasonable Standard of
Accommodation
Unless otherwise agreed by the Local
Planning Authority reserved matters
applications for each phase shall
demonstrate that all the residential units will
be constructed as far practicable to meet the
standards contained within the 'London
Housing Design Guide' published by the
Mayor of London.

Condition : 33 - 'No residential development shall take place until the bus depot is re-provided on the site in accordance with the application or the bus depot use on the site has permanently ceased and the land on which the bus depot is proposed to be sited has with the agreement of the Council been transferred to the Council.'

Condition : 34 - Energy Centre
Upon the completion of the final residential
unit within the Brent Lock West
development the Brent Lock West Energy
Centre shall be installed and operational and
shall thereafter be the sole heat supply
point for the Brent Lock West District
Heating network.

Condition : 35 - Commercial Deliveries
No commercial deliveries shall be taken at
or dispatched from the site outside the
hours of 07.00 hours to 22.00 hours Monday
to Saturday nor at any time on Sundays,
Bank or Public Holidays.

Condition : 36 - Compliance with Outline Application
The details submitted in relation to
Conditions 37, 38 and 39 shall be in
accordance with requirements of the
following approved plans and documents:
a) Document SD2: Development
Specification and Place-Making
Principles (as amended 7th February
2011); and
b) Document SD3 Regulatory Plans (as
amended 7th February 2011).

Condition : 37 - Approval of Reserved Matters Relating to
Layout, Scale, Access and Appearance
Prior to the commencement of development
for each phase, the following Reserved
Matters shall be submitted to and approved
in writing by the Local Planning Authority
for that phase:
a) layout;
b) scale;
c) access; and
d) appearance (excluding materials)
The details of access submitted shall be in
accordance with the site wide Access
Strategy provided in relation to Condition
10.
The development shall conform to the
details so approved.

Condition : 38 - Details of Materials
Prior to the erection of the superstructure
on each phase of development, details of
materials (including all materials samples)
to be used in that phase shall be submitted
to and approved in writing by the Local
Planning Authority and the development
shall be implemented in accordance with the
details so approved.

Condition : 39 - Reserved Matter - Landscaping
Prior to the erection of the superstructure
on each phase of development, details
(Reserved Matters) of landscaping for that
phase, including a strategy for
implementation shall be submitted to and
approved by the Local Planning Authority
for that phase. The landscape details
submitted shall accord with the Landscape
Strategy approved under Condition 11 and
shall include all:
a) hard landscape details at an
appropriate scale to include proposed
finished levels or contours, means of
enclosure, on street car parking
layouts, other vehicle and pedestrian
access and circulation areas, all hard
surfacing materials, minor artefacts
and structures
b) soft landscape details at an
appropriate scale to include planting
plans, written specifications
(including cultivation and other
operations associated with plant and
grass establishment), plant schedules
(noting species, plant sizes and
proposed numbers/densities), and
tree pits and species proposed to be
planted therein and measures to
ensure protection from services
routes.; and
c) samples of all landscaping materials.
All landscape works shall be carried out in
accordance with the approved details within
12 months of occupation of any buildings
within the relevant phase and retained
thereafter.

Condition : 40 - Details Required for Each Phase
Prior to the commencement of development
for each phase and support of the
information submitted under Condition 36
details of the following shall be submitted to
the Local Planning Authority for approval:
a) an illustrative build-out plan providing
the information set out within section
10.1 of Document SD2;
b) a Design and Access Statement;
c) a statement setting out how the
drainage strategy required by
Conditions 6 and 7 shall be
implemented for that phase;
d) a statement setting out how the
Remediation Strategy required by
Condition 5 shall be implemented for
that phase;
e) a statement setting out the following
information required by Condition 8
for that phase: the results of the
programme of archaeological work
including field evaluation; and a
subsequent mitigation strategy.
f) an Energy Statement, including the
location of photovoltaic panels as
required by the plan agreed under
Condition 14 where relevant;
g) details of the location of the green
roofs, as required by the plan agreed
under Condition 15.
h) a Sustainable Design and
Construction Statement providing
details of the approach to sustainable
design and construction for that
phase, which shows how it will meet a
minimum of Code Level 4 and/ or
BREEAM ?Very Good?; and
i) a Daylight, Sunlight and
Overshadowing Assessment to
comply with the requirements set out
within Condition 45.

The details required under b), c), d), e), f), g),
h) and i) shall then be implemented as
approved before the part of the development
to which it relates is first occupied, unless
otherwise agreed with the Local Planning
Authority.

Condition : 41 - Maximum Floor Areas and Land Uses
The maximum floorspace area to be
provided in each phase shall not result in
the maxima set out within Tables 3.2 to 3.11
of Document SD2 (provided at Appendix x)
being exceeded for the Development Zone
as a whole.

Condition : 42 - Distribution of Uses
The distribution of uses within each phase
shall be in accordance with the Regulatory
Plans (Document SD3) hereby approved
unless otherwise approved in writing by the
local planning authority pursuant to this
condition.

Condition : 43 - Minimum Communal Amenity Space
Requirements
The area of communal courtyard space to be
provided in each phase shall not result in
the provision of less communal courtyard
space than the amount set out within Table
3.14 of Document SD2 (provided at
Appendix x) for that Development Zone as a
whole.

Condition : 44 - Car Parking Provision
Car Parking for each phase shall be
provided in accordance with Regulatory
Plan 12a or such 'temporary' car parking
layout as may be agreed in writing by the
local planning authority provided that no
subsequent phase of the development shall
result in the removal of that ?temporary?
arrangement unless another ?temporary?
arrangement has been agreed or unless the
car parking provision for the completed
development complies with Regulatory Plan
12 a.

Condition : 45 - Ensuring a Good Standard of
Accommodation
The Daylight, Sunlight and Overshadowing
Assessment required by Condition 40I) shall
provide details of how the proposed design
applies the guidance within the Building
Research Establishment?s ?Site Layout
Planning for Daylight and Sunlight: A Guide
to Good Practice 1991?.

Condition : 46 - Noise
No development shall take place on each
phase until details have been submitted to
and approved by the Local Planning
Authority for a scheme of acoustic
insulation and any other necessary means
of ventilation provided. The resulting
internal noise environment provided for the
residential units shall not exceed the ?good?
limits contained in BS8233:1999, these
being: LAeq,16hour = 30 dB in living rooms;
a night (07:00-23:00) LAeq,8hour = 30 dB
and LAFmax = 45 dB in bedrooms; and a
night LAeq,1hour = 45dB in Kitchens,
Bathrooms and Utility Rooms. The details
shall be carried out as approved before the
dwellings to which they relate are first
occupied.

Condition : 47 - Plant and Equipment
Details of any external ventilation
equipment, including ducting, shall be
submitted to and approved in writing by the
Local Planning Authority before installation
and the development shall conform to the
details so approved before it is first
occupied.

Condition : 48 - Sustainable Construction
The Sustainable Design and Construction
Statement required by Condition 40h) shall
provide detail of how the development
within that phase shall comply with the
"essential" standards for materials in the
Mayor's Sustainable Design and
Construction SPG. These being- 50% timber
and timber products from Forest
Stewardship Council (FSC) source and
balance from a known temperate source.-
Insulation materials containing substances
known to contribute to stratospheric ozone
depletion or with the potential to contribute
to global warming must not be used.-
Minimize use of new aggregates- Reduce
waste during construction and demolition
phases and sort waste stream on site where
practical -Specify use of reused or recycled
construction materials -minimising solar
gain in summer (Policy 4A.10) - minimising
water use (Policy 4A.16) -protecting and
enhancing green infrastructure- outdoor
lighting should be energy efficient and
minimize light lost to sky.- All boilers
installed must be low NOx boilers,
conforming to at least NOX class 5.

Condition : 49 - Renewable Energy
The Energy Statement required by Condition
40f) shall provide details of a scheme for
reducing carbon emissions from the
completed phase by at least 20%, by the onsite
generation of renewable energy, unless
it can be demonstrated that such provision
is not feasible.

Condition : 50 - Landscape Management Plan
A landscape management plan, including
long term design objectives, management
responsibilities and maintenance schedules
for all hard and soft landscape areas, and
details of any temporary landscaping
(including boundary treatment) to be
provided and management thereof pending
the redevelopment of future phases of the
development, shall be submitted to and
approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority prior to the occupation of each
phase of the development to the west of the
Canal i.e. excluding Robin Grove Recreation
Ground, unless otherwise approved in
writing by the Local Planning Authority. The
maintenance schedule shall be for a
minimum period of ten years and include
details of the arrangements for its
implementation. The landscape
management plan shall be carried out as
approved unless otherwise approved in
writing by the Local Planning Authority.

Condition : 51 - Replacement Tree
If within a period of ten years from the date
of planting any tree or specimen shrub, that
tree or specimen shrub, or any tree or
specimen shrub planted in replacement for
it, is removed, uprooted or destroyed or dies
(or becomes, in the opinion of the Local
Planning Authority, seriously damaged or
defective), another tree or specimen shrub
of the same species and size as that
originally planted shall be planted at the
same place, unless the Local Planning
Authority gives its written approval to any
variation. (b) If within a period of ten years
from the date of occupation of any phase
any existing tree or specimen shrub within
the relevant phase which is to be retained in
accordance with the approved plans and
particulars is removed, uprooted or
destroyed or dies (or becomes, in the
opinion of the Local Planning Authority,
seriously damaged or defective), another
tree or specimen shrub shall be planted at
the same place and that tree or specimen
shrub shall be of such size and species, and
shall be planted at such time, as specified in
writing by the Local Planning Authority.

Condition : 52 - Waste and Recyling
No development shall take place in any
phase until a scheme for the storage and
collection of waste and materials to be
recycled in that phase has been submitted
to and approved in writing by the Local
Planning Authority and the approved
scheme shall then be managed as approved
unless otherwise approved in writing by the
Local Planning Authority.

Condition : 53 - Mitigation in accordance with ES
Prior to the commencement of development
of each phase, details of the mitigation
measures outlined in the Environmental
Statement relevant to that phase shall be
submitted to and approved by the Local
Planning Authority and carried out as
approved.

Condition : 54 - Footbridge Design
Prior to the implementation of the relevant
phase of development, as defined by the
phasing plan to be agreed under Condition
3, a scheme for the design of the footbridge
to accord with the parameters outlined
within the Footbridge Design &
Development Document Consideration
document (Section 7 of Document SD2)
shall be submitted to and approved in
writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Thereafter the bridges shall be constructed
as set out in the approved scheme.

Condition : 55 - Construction Impacts of the Footbridge
A Method Statement for the construction of
the footbridge shall be submitted to and
agreed in writing by the Local Planning
Authority prior to the implementation of the
relevant phase of development, as defined
by the phasing plan to be agreed under
Condition 3. Construction shall conform
to the details so agreed.

Condition : 56 - Compensatory Habitat Provision to Mitigate
the Impacts of the Footbridge
Prior to the implementation of the relevant
phase of development, as defined by the
phasing plan to be agreed under Condition
3, a scheme for the provision and
management of compensatory habitat shall
be submitted to and improved in writing by
the local planning authority. Thereafter the
development shall be implemented in
accordance with the approved scheme.

Condition : 57 - Buffer Zone
Prior to the implementation of the relevant
phase of development, as defined by the
phasing plan to be agreed under Condition
3, a scheme for the provision and
management of a buffer zone alongside this
part of the River Brent, shall be submitted to
and agreed in writing by the local planning
authority. Thereafter the development shall
be carried out in accordance with the
approved scheme and any subsequent
amendments shall be agreed in writing with
the local planning authority. The scheme
shall include:
? plans showing the extent and layout of the
buffer zone
? details of the planting scheme (for
example, native species)
? details demonstrating how the buffer zone
will be protected during development and
managed/maintained over the longer term
? details of any footpaths, fencing, lighting
etc.

Condition : 58 - Noise mitigation for the Bus Depot
Prior to the commencement of development
of the Bus Depot, a strategy for the
mitigation of noise emissions from the bus
depot shall be submitted to and approved in
writing by the Local Planning Authority. The
mitigation measures shall then be
implemented in accordance with the details
approved before the depot is brought into
use and maintained for the lifetime of the
building, unless otherwise agreed in writing
by the Local Planning Authority.

Condition : 59 - Hours of Use
The use of A3/A4 uses shall not be used
outside the hours 7am-11pm Monday ?
Saturday and 10am-11pm Sundays

Condition : 60 - Control of Noise, Fumes and Odours
The phase that includes the Class A3/A4
(Restaurant and Caf?) D1 uses shall not
commence until a scheme for the control of
noise, fumes and odours from the uses
concerned including details of sound
attenuation for any necessary plant and a
detailed assessment of the effectiveness of
the scheme has been submitted to and
approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority. The scheme once approved shall
be implemented before the caf? use shall
commence and be retained thereafter unless
otherwise approved in writing by the Local
Planning Authority.

Condition : 61 - Amplified Music
No amplified or other music played in or
from the Class A3/A4
(Restaurants/Caf?s/Bar) or D1 uses shall be
audible outside of the premises without the
prior written approval of the Local Planning
Authority.
